frontend.react: React / Next.js SPA or SSR web app
frontend.server_rendered: Server-rendered HTML templates (Django, Rails, Laravel views)
frontend.none: No web frontend needed (API-only, CLI, batch job, or mobile-only)
frontend.other: None of these fit well; the requirements need something not listed

backend.node: Node.js / TypeScript (Express, NestJS), good for real-time and JS teams
backend.python: Python (Django, FastAPI), good for data, ML, and quick CRUD
backend.java: Java / Kotlin (Spring Boot), large enterprise, regulated systems
backend.ruby: Ruby on Rails, fast MVP CRUD apps
backend.php: PHP (Laravel), content sites and cheap hosting
backend.other: None of these fit well; the requirements need something not listed

database.postgres: PostgreSQL, relational data with integrity and reporting
database.mysql: MySQL / MariaDB, relational, common web apps
database.redis: Redis as primary store, ephemeral or very low-latency data
database.timeseries: Time-series DB (TimescaleDB, InfluxDB), metrics, IoT, sensor data
database.sqlite: SQLite, embedded, single-user or offline apps
database.warehouse: Data warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake), analytics over large datasets
database.other: None of these fit well; the requirements need something not listed

hosting.azure: Azure, Microsoft ecosystem and enterprise compliance
hosting.gcp: Google Cloud, data and ML workloads
hosting.paas: PaaS (Vercel, Heroku, Render), small teams wanting zero ops
hosting.on_prem: On-premises / private data center, strict data residency or air-gapped
hosting.other: None of these fit well; the requirements need something not listed

mobile.pwa: Progressive web app instead of store apps
mobile.other: None of these fit well; the requirements need something not listed

platform.check: Can you tell what kind of product this is: a website or web app (including portals, storefronts, dashboards), a phone app, a desktop app, or a backend API? Answer yes if the product type is stated or clearly implied; answer no if it just says 'app', 'software', 'tool' or 'platform' without saying where it runs.

scale.check: Do the requirements indicate the expected number of users or traffic volume?

data.check: Can you infer the main kind of data this software would store, such as orders, bookings, user profiles, patient or business records, posts and photos, sensor readings, or analytics events? Answer no only if the purpose is too vague to guess the data.
data.ask: What data does it mainly store?
